question: I got a parking ticket. How do I pay it or contest it?

nuggets.text: State law lets localities enforce parking citations, including towing or immobilising vehicles with unpaid citations.
nuggets.quote: trailer parked on the public highways or public grounds against which there are three or more unpaid or otherwise unsettled parking violation notices may be removed to a place within such county, city, or town or in an adjacent locality designated by the chief law-enforcement officer for the temporary storage of the

nuggets.text: In Charlottesville parking tickets are paid to the City Treasurer.
The lower fine and any appeal are due within 96 hours.
nuggets.quote: Find the violation code on the ticket and look it up on the city's Violation Fees table. Every fine has a lower amount if paid within 96 hours and a doubled amount after 96 hours. Appeals are also due within 96 hours.

nuggets.text: A ticket can be contested in General District Court.
nuggets.quote: After 5 days the city forwards the case to the court and court costs apply. State law requires the city to certify a contested parking ticket to the district court.
$10 to $180 if paid within 96 hours, $20 to $360 after 96 hours, depending on the violation (see fees)
